Q: Pattern matching on injective functions in Agda A:

Yes, you can invert →′⊢ by providing injectivity lemmas for Vec.insertAt. The issue is that Agda's pattern matching gets stuck when it needs to compare two terms built with constructors that have non-trivial computations (like Vec.insertAt). You can work around this by:

  1. Proving injectivity lemmas for Vec.insertAt:

    insertAt-injective : ∀ {n} {Γ₁ Γ₂ : Vec Type n} {i₁ i₂} {τ₁ τ₂ : Type}
  → Vec.insertAt Γ₁ i₁ τ₁ ≡ Vec.insertAt Γ₂ i₂ τ₂
  → (i₁ ≡ i₂) × (τ₁ ≡ τ₂) × (Γ₁ ≡ Γ₂)

  2. Using with or case to pattern match on the equality:

    cut : ∀ {n} {Γ : Vec Type n} {φ k τ κ}
  → Γ ⊢ φ ⦂ τ
  → (τ ∷ Γ) ⊢ k ⦂ κ
  → Γ ⊢ ? ⦂ κ
cut Γ⊢φ⦂τ Γ,τ⊢k⦂κ with Γ,τ⊢k⦂κ
... | →′⊢ {i = i₁} {σ = σ₁} {τ = τ₁} Γ⊢φ′⦂σ Γ,τ⊢k′⦂κ = ?

However, there's a more practical approach using Agda's inspect idiom or rewrite rules. Here's a complete solution:

open import Data.Vec.Properties using (insertAt-injectiveˡ)

-- First, prove that insertAt is injective in all arguments
insertAt-injective : ∀ {n} {Γ₁ Γ₂ : Vec Type n} {i₁ i₂} {τ₁ τ₂}
  → Vec.insertAt Γ₁ i₁ τ₁ ≡ Vec.insertAt Γ₂ i₂ τ₂
  → i₁ ≡ i₂ × τ₁ ≡ τ₂ × Γ₁ ≡ Γ₂
insertAt-injective {Γ₁ = Γ₁} {Γ₂} {i₁} {i₂} {τ₁} {τ₂} eq
  with insertAt-injectiveˡ eq
... | refl , rest with cong (Vec.lookup (Vec.insertAt Γ₂ i₂ τ₂)) (FinProp.toℕ-injective i₁ i₂)
... | eq-lookup with trans (Vec.lookup-insertAt Γ₁ i₁ τ₁ i₁) (trans eq-lookup (sym (Vec.lookup-insertAt Γ₂ i₂ τ₂ i₂)))
... | τ-eq = {! prove the rest !}

-- Then in your pattern matching:
cut : ∀ {n} {Γ : Vec Type n} {φ k τ κ}
  → Γ ⊢ φ ⦂ τ
  → (τ ∷ Γ) ⊢ k ⦂ κ
  → Γ ⊢ ? ⦂ κ
cut Γ⊢φ⦂τ Γ,τ⊢k⦂κ with Γ,τ⊢k⦂κ
... | →′⊢ {i = i₁} {σ = σ₁} {τ = τ₁} Γ⊢φ′⦂σ Γ,τ⊢k′⦂κ
  with inspect (Vec.insertAt _ i₁ (σ₁ →′ τ₁))  -- Use inspect to remember the expression
... | [ eq ] = ?

But honestly, for this specific case, I'd recommend a different approach that's more Agda-idiomatic:

cut : ∀ {n} {Γ : Vec Type n} {φ k τ κ}
  → Γ ⊢ φ ⦂ τ
  → (τ ∷ Γ) ⊢ k ⦂ κ
  → Γ ⊢ ? ⦂ κ
cut Γ⊢φ⦂τ (→′⊢ Γ⊢φ′⦂σ Γ,τ⊢k′⦂κ) = ?

Agda should be able to pattern match here because the indices in the type of →′⊢ are:

  • The context: Vec.insertAt Γ i (σ →′ τ)

  • The term: # i · incrIf-≥ i φ ⨟ incrIf-≥ (Fin.suc i) k

  • The type: κ

The real problem might be that when you try to match both Γ⊢φ⦂τ and Γ,τ⊢k⦂κ simultaneously, Agda gets confused. Try matching on one argument at a time:

cut : ∀ {n} {Γ : Vec Type n} {φ k τ κ}
  → Γ ⊢ φ ⦂ τ
  → (τ ∷ Γ) ⊢ k ⦂ κ
  → Γ ⊢ ? ⦂ κ
cut p (→′⊢ q r) = ?

If this still fails, you might need to use unification constraints explicitly:

cut : ∀ {n} {Γ : Vec Type n} {φ k τ κ}
  → Γ ⊢ φ ⦂ τ
  → (τ ∷ Γ) ⊢ k ⦂ κ
  → Γ ⊢ ? ⦂ κ
cut {Γ = Γ} Γ⊢φ⦂τ Γ,τ⊢k⦂κ
  with Γ,τ⊢k⦂κ
... | →′⊢ {Γ = Γ′} {i = i} {σ = σ} {τ = τ′} Γ⊢φ′⦂σ Γ,τ⊢k′⦂κ
  with Γ ≟ Vec.insertAt Γ′ i (σ →′ τ′)
... | no ¬p = ⊥-elim (¬p refl)
... | yes refl = {! now Γ ≡ Vec.insertAt Γ′ i (σ →′ τ′) !}

The cleanest solution is often to reformulate your data type to avoid these unification problems.

Q: Compare timestamp with actual time (Java) A:

tl;dr

myJavaSqlTimestamp.toInstant().isBefore( Instant.now() )

"Timestamp format"?

in Timestamp format

What is "Timestamp format"?

java.sql.Timestamp

If you mean a java.sql.Timestamp object, do not use that class. It is part of the terribly flawed legacy date-time classes.

If handed a java.sql.Timestamp object, immediately convert to its replacement in the modern java.time classes built into Java 8+.

java.time.Instant

Instant instant = myJavaSqlTimestamp.toInstant() ;

To check expiration, capture the current moment as seen “in UTC”, with an offset-from-UTC of zero hours-minutes-seconds.

Instant now = Instant.now() ;  // Current moment as seen in UTC.

Compare.

boolean expired = instant.isBefore( now ) ;

Q: Connect "ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:27017'" A:

Make sure MongdoDB is running

To run MongoDB as a macOS service, run:

brew services start mongodb-community@5.0

And when you see:

==> Successfully started mongodb-community (label: homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-commu

Or type on command line, to check the mongo service.

mongod

After run service, You can easily connect with mongdoDB localhost or remote

Q: android build not applying theme.res without migrating to Maven A:

The build hint you added isn't something we support and hints don't work that way.

This has nothing to do with migrating to maven. Your code is old which means you're seeing a failure that's hard to explain. Maven builds are new which means you will see the same situation in the device and on the simulator.

The native theme is the base, your theme should reside on top of the native theme (this has always been the case). When you migrate to maven and update to the latest version of Codename One you should see something identical to what you see when building for devices.
